English: Racing Patch
A makeshift oval of trampled earth and temporary stakes, marking the earliest attempts at organized racing in the steppe.
Wooden Track
Simple wooden planks and barriers laid along the course, improving safety and organization for both horses and spectators.
Spectator Stand
Rough wooden bleachers offer a better view for the tribe, fostering communal excitement and clan unity.
Chariot Yard
A small yard for the storage and maintenance of chariots and horses, professionalizing the racing tradition.
Stone Track
The course is now lined with fitted stones, reducing dust and allowing for more spectacular races.
Mosaic Finish Line
A dazzling mosaic marks the finish, drawing crowds from afar and increasing the renown of the hippodrome.
Circus Pavilion
A grand tented pavilion for nobles and honored guests, increasing the spectacle and prestige of the games.
Imperial Racing Hall
A magnificent stone hall for festivities and feasts, cementing the hippodrome as the heart of courtly and clan life.
Grandstand
Tiered stone seating circles the arena, allowing thousands to witness the spectacle and filling the steppe with celebration.
Byzantine Hippodrome
A true marvel: marble tiers, imperial loges, and mosaics, the greatest center of steppe sport and unity, drawing rivals and dignitaries from a thousand leagues.
